about.heading: A developer who understands how ~~businesses~~ actually run.
about.body:
I'm Adewunmi Erijide Adeniji, known online as **Primemaven**. I'm a full stack developer based in Lagos, and I enjoy turning messy, manual processes into simple software people want to use.

I'm the CEO and Founder of **MyPropifyNG**, a real estate platform that helps Nigerians find homes through verified listings, without the risk of fraud. I also run Rhadsoft Tech, my software company, where I build my own products and custom software for clients.

I'm also a TEDx speaker, and I speak at and moderate sessions at tech events. As the software developer at IEMA Standards Limited, an ISO certification and training company, I build the internal systems the business runs on.

blocks.heading: Finding a home in Nigeria shouldn't feel like a ~~gamble~~.
blocks.text: House hunters lose money to fake listings and fake agents, and there's no reliable way to check a property before paying. Trust in the market is low, and honest owners and agents suffer for it too.

items.title: Fake listings and properties that don't exist or aren't for rent.
Fake agents who collect inspection or agency fees and disappear.
Photos that don't match the real property.
No trusted information about safety, roads or amenities in an area.
Payments made outside any protected system, with no way to get money back.

items.title: Partner validation

Adewunmi Erijide Adeniji, known as Primemaven, is a full stack developer, founder and TEDx speaker based in Lagos, Nigeria. He builds software that fits how Nigerian businesses actually work.

He is the CEO and Founder of MyPropifyNG, a real estate platform launched in 2025 across Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt. MyPropifyNG puts every listing through a 3-stage verification process of document authentication, physical inspection and partner validation, helping renters, buyers and students find homes without the risk of fraud.

In 2021 he founded Rhadsoft Tech, a software studio with bases in Surulere and Ikorodu that designs and builds web platforms, mobile apps, ERP systems and AI solutions. Rhadsoft has delivered more than 50 projects for over 30 clients and runs its own products, including MyPropifyNG, BookoraNG, IkoroduSquare and BookMeNaija.

Adewunmi also leads the Ikorodu chapter of Zev Builders, the developer community of Zevop, where he helps local developers learn, build and ship. He speaks and moderates at technology and industry events on software, entrepreneurship and building tech in Nigeria.

posts.title: Why we verify every listing at MyPropifyNG
posts.excerpt: Property fraud costs Nigerian house hunters money and trust. Here's why MyPropifyNG checks every listing before it goes live, and how the 3-stage process works.
posts.body:
Ask anyone who has searched for a flat in Lagos, Abuja or Port Harcourt, and you'll hear a version of the same story. A listing that looked perfect online. An "agent" who asked for an inspection fee, then an agency fee, then stopped picking up calls. A property that either didn't exist or belonged to someone who had never heard of the deal.

When I started MyPropifyNG, I wanted to fix that problem first, before anything else. Not with better photos or a nicer search page, but with one simple rule: **no listing goes live until we've verified it.**

## The problem isn't search, it's trust

Nigeria doesn't lack property websites. What it lacks is a reliable way to know whether what you're looking at is real. When anyone can post a listing, people learn to assume the worst, and honest owners and agents suffer for it too, because seekers don't trust them either.

> A property platform is only as good as the trust people place in its listings.

## How our 3-stage verification works

1. **Document authentication.** We check title and ownership documents to confirm that the person listing a property has the right to rent or sell it.
2. **Physical inspection.** Someone visits the property to confirm it exists and matches its description and photos.
3. **Partner validation.** Trusted partners confirm the listing before it goes live, adding a final layer of protection.

Only after all three steps does a property appear on the platform with a verified badge.

## Why we made listing free

Verification takes effort, so it would be easy to charge for it. We chose not to. Listing on MyPropifyNG is free for owners and seekers, because we want genuine properties on the platform, not just the ones whose owners can afford to pay.

## What comes next

We're working on ProPifyAI, which will match people with suitable verified properties within 24 hours of a request, and we plan to grow beyond Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt to five major cities.

If you're looking for a home, or you have a property to list, visit [mypropify.com.ng](https://www.mypropify.com.ng/). And if you've been scammed while house hunting, I'd like to hear your story. It shapes what we build next.

posts.title: Off-the-shelf or custom software? A guide for Nigerian businesses
posts.excerpt: When should a Nigerian business buy ready-made software, and when should it build its own? A practical guide from five years of building software at Rhadsoft Tech.
posts.body:
One of the first questions clients ask me at Rhadsoft Tech is: "Should we just buy something, or should you build it for us?" It's a good question, and the honest answer is that it depends. Here's how I help businesses decide.

## When off-the-shelf software is the right choice

Ready-made tools make sense when your process is standard and the tool fits it well. Accounting basics, email, video calls and simple online stores are good examples. If a well-known tool does 90% of what you need, at a price you can afford in naira, use it.

## When custom software pays for itself

- **Your process is your advantage.** If the way you work is what makes you different, forcing it into a generic tool means giving that up.
- **Your team is working around the tool.** When staff keep spreadsheets on the side because the system "doesn't do it that way", you're paying for software and still working manually.
- **You're juggling several disconnected tools.** Client records in one place, invoices in another and HR in a third leads to duplicate work and errors.
- **Foreign pricing doesn't fit.** Per-user dollar pricing adds up quickly, and the cost rises every time the exchange rate moves.

> Good software should fit how your business actually works, not the other way round.

## A real example

For IEMA Standards Limited, an ISO certification and training company, we built CRMops, FINops and HRops: connected systems for client management, finance and HR. Instead of adapting to generic tools, the team now runs its day-to-day operations from one set of systems designed around its own processes.

## How to decide

1. Write down the three tasks that take your team the most time each week.
2. Check whether an existing tool handles all three well, without workarounds.
3. Compare the yearly cost of that tool with a one-time build plus maintenance.
4. Think about where your business will be in three years, not just today.

If you'd like a second opinion on your situation, [send me a message](/#contact). Sometimes the best advice I can give is not to build anything at all.

posts.title: 7 questions to ask before you hire a software developer in Nigeria
posts.excerpt: Hiring a developer or agency for your website or app? Ask these seven questions first to avoid delays, hidden costs and software you can't maintain.
posts.body:
A software project can transform a business, or it can drain money and time. Most failed projects I've been asked to rescue went wrong before a line of code was written, because the right questions weren't asked at the start. Here are seven to ask any developer or agency, including me.

## 1. Can I see work you've actually shipped?

Ask for live products you can open and use, not just screenshots. Ask what the developer personally built on each one.

## 2. How will you understand my business first?

A good developer asks a lot of questions about your customers, your staff and your current process before quoting. If someone quotes in five minutes, they're guessing.

## 3. What exactly is included in the price?

Get the scope in writing: features, number of revisions, hosting, domain and training. Unclear scope is the most common cause of disputes.

## 4. How often will I see progress?

Insist on regular demos of working software, weekly if possible. Seeing progress early lets you catch misunderstandings while they're cheap to fix.

## 5. Who owns the code and the accounts?

You should own your domain, hosting account and source code. Make sure this is agreed before work starts.

> If you don't control your domain and hosting, you don't fully control your business online.

## 6. What happens after launch?

Every system needs fixes, updates and security patches. Ask about support, response times and the cost of ongoing maintenance.

## 7. How will you handle payments and data security?

If your software takes payments or stores customer data, ask how it will be protected and which payment providers will be used.

Planning a project? [Tell me about it](/#contact) and I'll answer these questions for you upfront.
